- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- If model shows steady upward trend with no sentiment signal, check for mean reversion; if true outcome drops >3% from forecast peak, adjust downward by 1–2% per period.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and model shows strong upward trend, true outcome often reverses; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 2–3 periods.  
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows strong upward movement, sentiment may be lagging; adjust forecast up by 1–2% per period for next 3–5 days.
